title: Measurements of the Dust Properties in z ≃ 1-3 Submillimeter Galaxies with ALMA
question: To constrain the dust emissivity index and dust temperature in z ~ 1-3 870μm-selected sub-millimeter galaxies using systematic ALMA 2mm continuum observations combined with multi-wavelength far-infrared data.

what.value: ALMA Cycle 0 Band 7 (870 um) positions and flux densities of ALESS sources

evidence.quote: In Table [\[table_sources\]](#table_sources) (Appendix [7](#app_sources)), we list the prior positions and 870 μm fluxes of our ALESS sources obtained with ALMA Band 7 (cite: Hodge2013), along with our measured 2 mm Band 4 fluxes.

We define a ‘well-sampled subset’ of 27 sources for which we detect the 2mm emission at $\hbox{S/N}\ge4$ which also have high-S/N detections at 870μm and at 250μm from *Herschel*/SPIRE (cite: Swinbank2014)

what.value: Spectroscopic redshifts from near-IR spectroscopy, ALMA CO, and [CII]

evidence.quote: as well as spectroscopic redshifts from near-IR spectroscopy (cite: Danielson2017), ALMA CO (cite: Birkin2021) and \[CII\] (cite: Swinbank2012).

what.value: Photometric redshifts and MAGPHYS physical properties (predicted 2mm fluxes, dust masses, dust luminosities, SFRs, stellar masses)

evidence.quote: The properties of the 99 ALESS main SMGs are described in detail in (cite: Hodge2013; Swinbank2014; Simpson2014; daCunha2015; Danielson2017).

what.value: ALMA Band 3 (3.3 mm) continuum fluxes for 10 sources

evidence.quote: (we also include ALMA Band 3 at 3.3mm, available for 10 of our sources from (cite: Wardlow2018), and ALMA Band 8 at 0.63mm, available for two sources from (cite: Rybak2019)).

what.value: ALMA Band 8 (0.63 mm) continuum fluxes for 2 sources

evidence.quote: (we also include ALMA Band 3 at 3.3mm, available for 10 of our sources from (cite: Wardlow2018), and ALMA Band 8 at 0.63mm, available for two sources from (cite: Rybak2019)).

evidence.loc: 2 mm sources with no counterpart in the ALESS main catalog
evidence.quote: We find that four of these sources have a robust *Spitzer*/IRAC 3.6μm counterpart (within 0.5 arcsec) in the ECDFS IRAC-selected catalog of (cite: Damen2011), confirming they are likely to be real galaxies.

what.value: Local galaxy comparison samples (HRS, JINGLE, HERUS) for T_dust and beta

evidence.loc: Comparison with other measurements and theoretical predictions
evidence.quote: Both moderately star-forming local galaxies from the *Herschel* Reference sample (cite: Cortese2014) and the JCMT dust and gas In Nearby Galaxies Legacy Exploration (JINGLE) sample (cite: Lamperti2019), as well as local ultra-luminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs) from the HERUS sample (cite: Clements2018)

recipe.method: Fourier transform uv visibilities and deconvolve using the clean algorithm with Briggs weighting in CASA
key_parameters: robust = 0.5, image size = 166'' x 166'', pixel scale = 0.46''

recipe.goal: Extract 2mm source fluxes, stack non-detections, and apply flux deboosting
recipe.method: Blind source identification above 4 sigma using boxit and 2D Gaussian fitting with imfit; prior-position extraction for 1.5 <= S/N < 4; median stacking for S/N < 1.5; analytical deboosting for blind detections
key_parameters: 4 sigma threshold for blind detection; 1.5 <= S/N < 4 for prior extraction; deboosting factor B = 1 + 0.2 ([S/N]/5)^-2.3
assumptions: Sources are unresolved at ~2.3 arcsec resolution

recipe.goal: Analyze 870um-to-2mm flux ratios and test for redshift evolution
recipe.method: Compute S_nu[870um]/S_nu[2mm] ratios, evaluate Spearman rank correlations, and compare redshift slope against Monte Carlo trials from Casey et al. (2018a) Model B
key_parameters: Redshift range 1.2 < z < 5.0 for linear fit in log(1+z) vs flux ratio
assumptions: Casey et al. (2018a) Model B assumes fixed beta = 1.8 and no redshift evolution in T_dust

recipe.goal: Fit far-IR to millimeter dust SEDs to derive T_dust, beta, L_dust, and M_dust
recipe.method: Bayesian SED fitting of rest-frame lambda > 70 um photometry (Herschel/SPIRE 250, 350, 500 um and ALMA Bands 8, 7, 4, 3) using isothermal modified blackbody models (optically-thin and general opacity)
key_parameters: Priors: T_dust uniform in [15, 80] K, beta uniform in [1.0, 3.0], lambda_thick uniform in [60, 140] um (for general opacity)
assumptions: Isothermal dust grains in thermal equilibrium; kappa_0 = 0.77 cm^2 g^-1 at nu_0 = 353 GHz (850 um); LambdaCDM cosmology with H_0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Lambda = 0.7, Omega_m = 0.3; CMB heating and contrast corrections from da Cunha et al. (2013)

answer_key.quantity: Number of ALESS main catalog sources with measured 2mm flux density (S/N >= 1.5)

evidence.quote: We measure the flux densities for 70 sources, for which we obtain a typical 870μm-to-2mm flux ratio of $14\pm5$.

answer_key.quantity: Number of ALESS main catalog sources blindly detected at 2mm (S/N >= 4)

evidence.quote: Our source extraction procedure yields a total of 53 detections of ALESS main catalog sources with $\hbox{S/N}\ge4$ within the primary beam FWHM (i.e., sensitivity $>50\%$ of the maximum).

answer_key.quantity: 3-sigma 2mm flux density upper limit from median stack of 29 undetected ALESS sources

evidence.quote: The stack produces no detection, however it allows us to place a $3\sigma$ flux density upper limit of 0.045 mJy.

answer_key.quantity: Median 870um-to-2mm flux density ratio (for 70 detected SMGs)

evidence.quote: The median flux density ratio for the 70 SMGs for which we measure a 2 mm flux density is $S_\nu\mathrm{[870\hbox{\textmu m}]}/S_\nu\mathrm{[2mm]}=14\pm5$ (with the error indicating the standard deviation range; for the well-sampled subset, we find a median of $14\pm4$).

answer_key.quantity: Median 870um-to-2mm flux density ratio (full ALESS sample of 99 sources including upper limits)

evidence.quote: Accounting for the upper limits for non-detections, the median flux ratio of the full ALESS sample increases to $S_\nu\mathrm{[870\hbox{\textmu m}]}/S_\nu\mathrm{[2mm]}=17\pm9$.

answer_key.quantity: Median dust emissivity index beta (well-sampled subset of 27 SMGs, optically-thin model)

evidence.quote: For our well-sampled subset, we find median values of $\hbox{$T_\mathrm{dust}$}=30^{+14}_{-8}$ K, and $\beta=1.9\pm0.4$ for the stacked likelihood distributions (the errors are the 16th-84th percentile ranges of the stacked distributions).

answer_key.quantity: Median dust temperature T_dust (well-sampled subset of 27 SMGs, optically-thin model)

evidence.quote: For our well-sampled subset, we find median values of $\hbox{$T_\mathrm{dust}$}=30^{+14}_{-8}$ K, and $\beta=1.9\pm0.4$ for the stacked likelihood distributions (the errors are the 16th-84th percentile ranges of the stacked distributions).

answer_key.quantity: Median dust mass M_dust (well-sampled subset of 27 SMGs, optically-thin model)

evidence.quote: The median dust mass of our well-sampled SMGs from is $M_\mathrm{dust}=5.8^{+5.9}_{-2.4}\times10^8\,M_\odot$, consistent with previous estimates using MAGPHYS which also assume optically-thin dust and $\beta=1.5-2$ (though multiple temperature components), and no fluxes beyond 870μm (cite: daCunha2015).

answer_key.quantity: Spearman rank correlation coefficient between T_dust and beta (well-sampled subset)

evidence.quote: Fig. [10](#fig:2dstacked) shows that there is a negative correlation between the dust temperatures and emissivity indexes of our well-sampled sources ($r_\mathrm{S}=-0.66$, $3.4\sigma$), and a positive correlation between dust luminosity and temperature ($r_\mathrm{S}=0.73$, $3.7\sigma$; a similar correlation is also found, e.g., by (cite: daCunha2015)).

score_reason: The ALMA data are standard pipeline-calibrated continuum visibilities from a single public project (2015.1.00948.S), imaging parameters (task, robust, pixel scale, image size) and source extraction tasks (boxit, imfit, deboosting equation) are explicitly stated, and the Bayesian SED model equations and priors are fully described.
rediscovery_reason: Public archival ALMA Band 4 dataset with straightforward continuum imaging, source extraction, and analytical/Bayesian modified blackbody SED fitting yielding clear numeric answer keys (70 detections, median flux ratio 14+/-5, median beta 1.9+/-0.4, and individual parameters for 27 galaxies in Table 2).
